newsitem.title: USA: Clinton seeks $1 billion to improve air security.
newsitem.headline: Clinton seeks $1 billion to improve air security.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Monday called on Congress to provide $1 billion in funding to hire more FBI agents to fight terrorism and to broadly improve U.S. airline and airport security.

"Terrorists don't wait, and neither should we," Clinton told reporters at a White House ceremony where he received a report on enhancing airport security and urged the Congress to act before it adjourns in October.
Vice President Al Gore on Monday gave Clinton a report on tightening security in the U.S. aviation system that the president had sought after the July 17 explosion of TWA Flight 800 off New York.

Gore announced the report's key points last week, including a call for better bomb detection equipment, profiling passengers, matching passengers to their baggage, increased use of bomb-sniffing dogs and running background checks on employees with access to secure airport areas.
But the president said he wanted the money to go beyond the narrow issue of airline security, using it to fight terrorism more broadly at home and abroad.

"We must tighten protection at a number of high profile public sites, including government buildings, national landmarks and national parks," Clinton said. "These counter-terrorism funds are a smart investment in our nation's security and our people's safety."
